sources.name: Photo of the FITNESS SF sign, shared on Instagram (link from Mahir)

caption:
A FITNESS SF gym in the Bay Area put a new rule on its screen: don't vibe code in between sets.
The notice asks members to keep rest time for recovery, not React components, and to stop prompting AI during their workout.
Vibe coding, a term Andrej Karpathy coined in 2025, has officially reached the weight room.
Would you follow this rule, or check on your coding agent between sets?

slides.headline: A San Francisco gym had to post a new rule: *don't vibe code* between sets

image.credit: FITNESS SF sign, via social media

slides.heading: Rest is for *recovery*
paras: A screen inside a FITNESS SF gym lists a new rule under "Gym Etiquette 101": don't vibe code in between sets.
Members are told to keep their rest time for recovery, "not React components," and to stop checking commits or prompting AI mid-workout.

slides.heading: Lift harder. *Ship later.*
paras: The sign closes with a line any startup founder would recognize: "Be present. Lift harder. Ship later."
FITNESS SF is a family-run chain with gyms across San Francisco, Oakland and Marin, the same region where the big AI labs are based.

slides.heading: Where *vibe coding* came from
paras: OpenAI cofounder Andrej Karpathy coined the term in February 2025: tell an AI what you want and accept the code it writes, often without reading every line.

paras.t: Collins named it Word of the Year for 2025.
